exchanges: Hello! First proper evening in Leeds and the flat is finally quiet.
Glad it has settled down. How was the move?
Long. My mum Gwen drove me up from Cardiff and cried at every service station.
That sounds like an emotional drive for both of you.
She packed me a tub of cawl for the freezer because it's her favourite thing to make and eat.
That is a lovely taste of home to have on hand.
It is. My flatmate Priya has already been very welcoming.
A friendly flatmate makes the first week much easier.
She works part-time at Primark in town, so she's already sorted me out with a discount on bedding.
That is a useful perk in the first week.
Very useful. I've bought far too much stuff.
Most first-years do in the first few days.
Including a second-hand Brompton off a guy on the floor below.
Folding bikes are handy when space is tight.
My girlfriend Mariana thinks I've lost my mind.
She may come round once she sees how handy it is.
Doubt it. She's from Recife, so she thinks anything below twenty degrees is unliveable.
Winter here might be a shock for her then.
She's visiting in November, so we'll see.
Hopefully the weather is kind to her.
I joined the rowing club at the freshers' fair, which means 6am starts.
Early starts, but clubs like that are a great way to meet people.
My brother Rhys says I'll quit within a month.
Brothers do like to make predictions like that.
He's one to talk. He can't even commit to a car. He's just bought a Fiesta after swearing he'd never drive one.
Changing his mind seems to be a pattern.
Rhys has never changed his mind about the Bluebirds, though. Season ticket since he was twelve.
Some loyalties are permanent.
Our module lecturer is also called Priya, which made me laugh. Two Priyas on day one.
That will make for some confusing stories back home.
She worked at Arup for years before becoming a lecturer, so she has loads of real project stories.
Industry experience tends to make lectures more interesting.
Definitely. Obinna, who sits next to me, asked her about a hundred questions.
Sounds like he is keen.
He is. He told me his family is Igbo and his grandad was a surveyor.
That is a nice family connection to the subject.
Sorry, I got Rhys's car wrong earlier. He texted to say it's a Corsa, not a Fiesta.
Thanks for clearing that up.
He was quite offended.
Car loyalty runs deep for some people.
Apparently. My birthday is in February, so Mariana is already planning something.
That gives her plenty of time.
I hope it's not a surprise party. I hate those.
You could drop a gentle hint.
Good idea. Anyway, the kitchen is a disaster already.
A cleaning rota might help before it gets worse.
Someone left a pan of beans out for two days.
That is a classic shared kitchen problem.
I'll bring it up at the flat meeting.
A calm word at the meeting is the best way to handle it.
Remind me, where does my flatmate work?
Right, thanks.
No problem.
I still can't believe I'm doing geology. My school careers advisor told me to do law.
It sounds like you picked what you actually enjoy.

earlier_question.right_reply: Your flatmate Priya works part-time at Primark.
earlier_question.wrong_reply: Your flatmate Priya works part-time at Arup.

questions.message: What does my mum love cooking most?
Rhys has a Corsa now, doesn't he?
What subject am I studying again?
I think I'll make a cup of tea and do some reading before bed.
What food does Rhys like most?
Sorry, where does Priya from the flat work again?
